items.title: Muslims believe the Quran was revealed via the angel Gabriel
items.claim: How do Muslims understand the Quran's origin?

options.text: Muhammad's wise sayings, gathered over centuries
The direct word of God, revealed to Muhammad through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) over 23 years (610-632 CE), to be recited and transmitted unchanged in Arabic
A revised version of the Bible adapted for Arabia

items.reveal:
The word 'Quran' comes from the Arabic root q-r-' meaning 'to recite'. The first revelation (Sura 96, 'Iqra' — 'Recite!') is dated to around 610 CE at the Cave of Hira on Mount Jabal al-Nour.

The Quran was compiled in written form under the third caliph Uthman (around 650 CE), with non-conforming versions destroyed to ensure a single authoritative text. Muslims regard only the Arabic text as the Quran proper; translations are 'meanings of' the Quran.

The Hadith — sayings of Muhammad — is a separate category, compiled by his companions and successors. Major Sunni collections: Sahih al-Bukhari (d. 870) and Sahih Muslim (d. 875).
items.why: The Quran's status differs from how Christians understand the Bible. Islamic theology treats every Arabic word as direct divine speech — which is why translation is always 'the meaning of' rather than 'the Quran'.

items.title: The Five Pillars have a canonical order — beginning with Shahada
items.claim: What is the standard Sunni order of the Five Pillars of Islam?

options.text: Shahada (declaration of faith), Salah (five daily prayers), Zakat (almsgiving, 2.5% of accumulated wealth), Sawm (fasting in Ramadan), Hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca, once if able)

items.reveal:
The Hadith of Gabriel (recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) lists the Pillars in this order. The Shahada is the doorway — 'There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God'.

Shia Islam (Twelver tradition) frames obligations differently. They recognise the practices but as part of the Furu al-Din (Ten Ancillaries of the Religion), alongside jihad, enjoining good and forbidding wrong, tawalla (love of the household of the Prophet) and tabarra (disassociation from enemies).

Zakat is calculated annually on accumulated wealth above a threshold (nisab); Sawm requires no food, drink or marital relations from dawn (fajr) to sunset (maghrib) during Ramadan.
items.why: Religious practice has specific structure. Treating the Pillars as a vague list of good acts misses the theological logic — faith first, then prayer, then social action.

items.title: Every Sikh gurdwara serves langar — a free meal for all

options.text: A meal sold to support the gurdwara

A free communal meal served to anyone regardless of religion, caste, gender or background — a foundational Sikh practice originated by Guru Nanak and institutionalised by Guru Amar Das (3rd Guru), who required visitors to eat langar before meeting him

items.reveal:
Langar is served in the langar hall of every gurdwara worldwide. All sit on the floor at the same level — explicitly rejecting caste hierarchy. The Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar) serves around 100,000 meals daily; volunteers prepare and clean.

Guru Amar Das (1479-1574) made eating langar a requirement before meeting him — including for the Mughal Emperor Akbar, who reportedly sat with peasants before being granted an audience.

In the UK, Sikh organisations like Khalsa Aid extend the langar tradition to refugees, food banks and disaster response — in Ukraine, Turkey after the 2023 earthquake, and at UK floods.
items.why: Practice can teach doctrine. Sitting on the floor and eating together puts equality into the body — more direct than verbal teaching.
